correctness.rationale: Coprime quotient rule forces denominator logarithmic derivative K to be a positive integer; prime-exponent modular divisibility forces K a sum of positive integers. For omega(a)≤4, D(a)/a≤247/210, hence K=1 and b=q^q. Positive surpluses are exhausted by a=30, a=2·3·11·13, a=42s with s prime 11≤s<42, and a=30r with r prime≥7. Only the last can equal q^q, giving r=q^q−30. The converse follows from direct quotient differentiation. Standalone exact finite checker is a corroboration, not an infinite proof.
